items.verdict: in-Korea (change of sub-code), not abroad: visamap is right, visadocs 'within' is wrong
items.detail:
Every source I could reach treats bachelor's to master's as something done inside Korea. Universities file it for their students before the semester starts. SNU's group filing (2024 fall) lists it as a 체류자격 변경 from D-2-2 to D-2-3. JNU's D-2 guide lists 상위과정 진학 (D22→D23, D23→D24) among its extension applicants (from 4 months before expiry). A JNU notice says school changes are 원칙적으로 불가 but allowed for 상위과정 진학. No source I found says to leave Korea for an upward move, and none limits it to the same university.

The visadocs 'within' rule (use: abroad, notice 'to go on to a higher course, you leave Korea') has no Korean text or line ref, unlike the downward 'report' rule, which cites 등록사항 변경신고 › 하위 학위과정 이동의 예외적 허용 (txt 1995–2004). visadocs also contradicts itself: its 'exceptions' entry gives in-Korea use: change for 'higher course at the same university'. The manual section title implies the 'restricted in principle' rule is about moving DOWN a course, so the 'within' notice looks like an inverted reading of that rule.

Limits: I could not open the 2026.9.18 manual text itself (search only), so the manual wording is inferred, not quoted. Whether the office books the move as a status change or as an extension with the new sub-code varies (SNU vs JNU), but both happen in Korea. Gaps: SNU warns that if your stay ends before the degree is conferred, the deadline differs, so check with immigration first. With a gap after graduation the reader would normally go through D-10-1 or apply anew; I found no source for a 'same university only' or 'graduating student only' rule.

items.verdict: in-Korea (change of sub-code / extension), not abroad: visamap is right, visadocs 'within' is wrong
items.detail:
Same finding as D-2-2>D-2-3. JNU names master's to doctorate (D23→D24) explicitly as an in-Korea extension case for students going on to a higher course. SNU's group filings cover graduate sub-code changes made in Korea before the semester starts.

The visadocs 'within' rule (use: abroad) has no Korean source text. It is contradicted by visadocs' own 'exceptions' entry (same university: use change) and appears to invert the manual's restriction on moving DOWN a course (등록사항 변경신고 › 하위 학위과정 이동의 예외적 허용).

Common real-world cases: a 석사 졸업(예정)자 going straight on to a 박사 course, and a 석·박사 통합과정 (that is D-2-4 from the start, so no move is needed). Without a gap the reader applies in Korea with the new standard admission letter before the current stay ends. I found no evidence that the move is limited to the same university or to students about to graduate. I could not open the 2026 manual's own wording (search only).

items.verdict: in-Korea (change of sub-code), not abroad: likely right in visamap; weaker evidence
items.detail:
No source I found requires leaving Korea for an upward degree move. The JNU notice says a D-2 student cannot in principle change school, except when going on to a higher course. That covers the usual associate-degree route: transferring to a 4-year university (편입), or a 전공심화과정 at the same college, which is D-2-2 by definition (학사학위 및 전공심화과정).

The visadocs 'within' use: abroad has no Korean source text and contradicts visadocs' own same-university 'change' exception. The 'restricted in principle' wording belongs to downward moves (하위 학위과정 이동의 예외적 허용, a report).

The evidence is weaker than for D-2-2>D-2-3. The university pages I found name D22→D23 and D23→D24 but not D21→D22 explicitly. I could not read the 2026 manual text, so the docs page should drop the abroad default but stay cautious. Same timing caveat: apply before the current stay ends and before the semester. With a gap after graduation, D-10-1 or a new application from abroad is the usual path.
